content.text:
The flight ended on schedule: both ad groups had end times of July 16 at 00:00 Mountain, and the campaign is no longer serving.

**Larchmorrow Strength recap, July 11–15, 2027 (Mountain time)**

| | Spend | Impressions | Link clicks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Post 2206282024354198610 ("A little strength can fit into a summer day…") | $245.16 | 196,565 | 109 |
| Post 2206463218284357170 ("Your summer calendar…") | $246.79 | 212,547 | 127 |
| **Total** | **$491.95** | **409,112** | **236** |

- **Budget:** $491.95 of the $500.00 was spent. Nothing else was launched.
- **Setup:** I ran one campaign with two ad groups, one for each approved post. They were set to the link-clicks goal and targeted the US and Canada on iOS and Android only. I left the age targeting open, since there's no sign-up age limit.
- **Optimization:** I checked on July 13. The two posts were performing about the same, so I made no changes.
- **Which post did better:** The "calendar" post got somewhat more clicks, about 0.060% of impressions versus 0.055% for the other. That gap is small, and I wouldn't treat it as a clear winner.
- **What the figures show:** Impressions and link clicks show how many people saw the ads and tapped through to larchmorrow.com/start. They don't show trial starts. X can't see those, because the site has no X pixel and trials start inside the app.
- **Trial starts:** To judge how well the campaign worked, compare your in-app trial starts for July 11–15 against the 236 clicks and $491.95 spend. Cost per trial start is spend divided by that count.
